summary: Keepalive proxy affinity causing uneven tenant quota accounting and intermittent 429s
description: Issue summary: NexusAI (private VPC deployment) reports intermittent 429s for a subset of API keys after onboarding a custom keepalive proxy that pins upstream connections. Impact: customer-facing production traffic experiences short windows of elevated 429s (5-15 minutes) affecting several high-priority endpoints (streams and embeddings). Observed pattern is tenant-scoped: some API keys on the tenant hit throttles while others operate normally.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy NexusAI's HTTP reverse proxy (configured to reuse long-lived keepalive connections to Redwood edge).
2) Fan out 50 short-lived client streams across 10 worker processes behind the proxy.
3) Observe request rate and per-key 429s in /v1/chat/stream and /v1/embeddings over ~10 minutes.
observed_behavior:
- Short windows of tenant-scoped 429s that correlate with proxy connection affinity and connection reuse.
- Throttle headers show remaining:0 for affected keys while other keys show remaining>0.
- Console shows uneven per-route token accounting on the gateway despite even incoming request distribution.
expected_behavior: Request accounting should be uniform across keys; proxy connection reuse should not cause persistent per-key quota starvation or double-counting.
logs_and_headers:
- Sample response headers from affected request: x-rate-limit-limit: 60000, x-rate-limit-remaining: 0, x-rate-limit-reset: 23
- NexusAI provided proxy nginx access logs showing single upstream connection handling many distinct client IPs with connection-pinning enabled (keepalive requests reused connection to same backend socket).
impact: Customer reports degraded feature availability for key product flows (search re-ranker and document ingestion). Business impact: partial user-facing degradation during bursts; NexusAI has flagged as P1 due to revenue-sensitive pipelines.
workaround_proposed: Short-term: ask NexusAI to disable connection pinning / reduce keepalive reuse (set smaller keepalive_reuse or use proxy buffering) to force per-request upstream reconnections. As a mitigation ask they spread API keys across multiple upstream connections or introduce small jitter in worker start times.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Connection-pinning causes the gateway to attribute refill tokens to the first API key on the reused upstream socket, leading to starvation for other keys sharing the socket.
Hypothesis B: Proxy reuse triggers an edge-layer optimization (sticky-session) that collapses per-request accounting windows into a single connection bucket.

Checks performed: replicated traffic with simulated nginx keepalive pool; instrumented gateway to log connection_id -> api_key mapping; observed that connection_id persisted across client IPs and associated with a single token bucket in our accounting layer.
Dashboards referenced: RateLimiter/PerTenant/TokenDistribution (link internal), Edge/ConnectionAffinity/Histogram, Customer/NexusAI/Throttles-2026-03-10.

Partial finding: When upstream sockets are long-lived and first-seen key is high-volume, remaining counters show 0 for other keys until connection TTL refresh; confirms per-connection attribution bug.
Risks: Changing gateway accounting requires careful rollout to avoid double-counting during migration; billing must be aligned for windows where counts may shift.

Next steps: prepare feature-flagged gateway patch, create roll-forward migration plan with canary on dedicated private tenant infra, and publish short-term proxy configuration guidance for private customers.
resolution_notes: In progress. Short-term guidance shared with NexusAI: disable upstream connection pinning, set keepalive_timeout=30s, set proxy_http_version 1.1 and set upstream_keepalive to a lower value to reduce socket reuse. Long-term fix: feature-flagged gateway change to attribute tokens per-request rather than per-connection; PR referenced in INT-5544. Billing team to reconcile any anomalous usage for the affected window.
